pool.text: Juan de Salazar de Espinosa established a fort named Asunción.
Founding document names city "Nuestra Señora de la Asunción".
Priest described colonists' licentious life as "paradise of Muhammad".
First Synod of Asunción set evangelization guidelines in Guaraní.
Uprising under José de Antequera y Castro challenged Spanish rule.
Rebels forced governor Velasco to surrender, achieving independence.
Asunción served as relief center during Chaco War.
Treaty of Asunción signed with Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay.
Asunción became autonomous municipality, not part of any department.
Castelvi House restored and became City Memory Museum.
Formal closure of Asunción tram system in November.
Congress building attacked by tanks during failed coup.
Modern building opened to house Congress.
Ycua Bolaños supermarket fire killed over 400 people.
Selection of seven cultural heritage treasures took place in Asunción.
Avenida Costanera Norte inaugurated during bicentennial celebrations.
Impeachment of President Lugo caused Paraguay's suspension from Mercosur.
Political crisis saw protesters set fire to Congress building.
1.6 million foreign tourists arrived, generating over US$600 million earnings.
First stage of Parque Lineal Costanera opened with bike lanes and amenities.
